No additional precomputed pyramid structures are stored in memory for the culling logic itself; the hierarchy is accessed on-demand [S1].

The claim states that no additional precomputed pyramid structures are stored in memory for the culling logic and that the hierarchy is accessed on-demand. Source [S1] explicitly contrasts MIP mapping, which 'precomputes image pyramids... and stored on disk', with the IDX format used in the described system. It states that IDX 'provides multiresolution access without storing these pyramids' and that the technique involves 'loading only the spatial extent and resolution necessary for the current camera view'. This confirms that the system does not store precomputed pyramids (like MIP maps) but instead accesses the necessary data levels on-demand based on the view.
supported

Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
